description: I’m a cross-disciplinary creator working with AI, design, data, content, and event optimization. For NASA Space Apps 2026, I want to build an AI web app using NASA data to help farmers understand environmental risks and make better decisions. Looking for teammates in AI/ML, data analysis, agriculture, climate, web development, or UI/UX. Let’s build a practical and engaging prototype together.
summary: FarmShift AI is an interactive agricultural decision-support application designed to help farmers explore climate-adaptive crop rotation strategies. By integrating NASA Earth observation data with local soil conditions, crop characteristics, and farmer priorities, the platform compares alternative farming strategies through transparent environmental indicators and explainable analysis. It aims to support better-informed decisions about soil management, water conservation, and agricultural resilience. Rather than replacing farmers or agronomists, FarmShift AI makes complex environmental information easier to understand and apply to agricultural planning.
details:
FarmShift AI

Project Overview

FarmShift AI is an interactive agricultural decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.

The project explores how Earth observation data, local soil information, crop characteristics, and farmer priorities can be combined to support climate-adaptive crop rotation planning.

How It Works

Users create a farm profile by entering their location, farm size, soil conditions, current crops, irrigation availability, and agricultural priorities.

The application integrates relevant NASA environmental datasets, including soil moisture and precipitation information where available.

It then compares alternative crop rotation strategies based on environmental suitability, water considerations, soil management, crop diversity, and potential climate-related risks.

An explainable decision-support interface presents the reasoning, supporting information, assumptions, and limitations behind each strategy.

Innovation

The main innovation is connecting NASA Earth observation data with practical agricultural planning.

Instead of displaying environmental data alone, the application translates relevant indicators into understandable comparisons that farmers can explore.

Users can also adjust farming priorities and examine how different environmental scenarios may affect the relative suitability of alternative strategies.

Expected Impact

The project aims to make environmental information more accessible to agricultural decision-makers, encourage informed soil and water management, and support exploration of more climate-resilient farming practices.

Technology and Tools

The planned technology stack includes React, TypeScript, interactive data visualization, NASA data APIs, and AI-assisted development tools.

Actual datasets, API integrations, and implemented functions will be documented transparently in the final version.

Limitations

The application is a decision-support prototype, not a validated crop-yield prediction system.

Its recommendations depend on data availability, input quality, agricultural assumptions, and local conditions. Further validation by agronomists and field testing would be necessary before practical deployment.

Originality and AI Disclosure

The project concept, design decisions, application structure, and final integration are developed as original project work. AI-assisted tools are used for development support and will be disclosed according to NASA Space Apps requirements.
